forces.title: Policy support to boost local gold refining capacity
forces.description: The government proposes a policy to increase gold supply from local refineries to 80% from the current 40% within the next few years. This initiative aims to reduce import reliance and strengthen domestic gold processing capabilities, providing a significant tailwind for the gold refining segment (IN020401) within Precious Metals & Gems by enhancing local value addition and reducing external dependencies.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Gold prices in durable high-price regime
forces.description: Gold prices have entered a structurally higher regime, driven by sustained central bank buying, robust investment demand, and geopolitical uncertainty. This provides a strong revenue tailwind for gold mining, processing, and refining companies (IN020401), improving their profitability and investment attractiveness as their primary output commands higher market prices over the long term.
forces.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

forces.title: Lab-grown diamonds (LGDs) intensifying competition for natural diamonds
forces.description: The rise of Lab-Grown Diamonds (LGDs), offered at significant discounts and boasting ethical appeal, is a structural shift disrupting the natural diamond market. Retailers are embracing LGDs for better margins and strong consumer demand, creating intense competition for traditional natural diamonds sourced from mining. This trend exerts downward pressure on demand and prices for rough natural diamonds (IN020404 output).

forces.title: Decline in rough diamond production to historical lows
forces.description: Global rough diamond production significantly decreased in CY23 and CY24, reaching the lowest levels since the Kimberly Process began data publication (excluding COVID-19 lockdown year). This reduction, driven by market stabilization efforts and falling demand for natural stones due to LGD competition, represents a supply-side headwind for the diamond mining segment (IN020404), constraining output and revenue potential.

forces.title: High reliance on gold imports due to domestic supply-demand gap
forces.description: India's gold industry faces a significant supply-demand gap, with domestic production covering only 18% of total consumption in CY24. This heavy reliance on imports exposes the domestic gold mining, processing, and refining sector (IN020401) to global price volatility, supply chain disruptions, and foreign exchange risks, hindering self-sufficiency and economic stability for the sector.

forces.title: Underdeveloped domestic gold mining sector due to regulatory and infrastructure challenges
forces.description: India's gold mining sector (IN020401) is significantly underdeveloped, hampered by persistent regulatory challenges, cumbersome licensing processes, and inadequate infrastructure in potential mining regions. These systemic issues impede new investments, delay exploration efforts, and increase operational costs, thereby limiting the growth and output of domestic gold mining and processing operations.

forces.title: Significant expansion of gold refining capacity in India
forces.description: India's gold refining capacity (IN020401) has expanded substantially, growing from fewer than 5 refineries in CY13 to 33 in CY21. This structural growth in refining infrastructure supports the domestic gold processing segment, reducing reliance on external refining and enhancing the value chain within India, aligning with self-reliance objectives despite challenges in upstream mining.

forces.title: Government reforms to boost gold mining and processing
forces.description: Recent government reforms, including amendments to the Mines and Minerals Act, the National Mineral Policy, and auctioning mining blocks, aim to encourage domestic production and private sector involvement in gold mining and processing (IN020401). These measures are designed to attract investment and exploration, creating a favorable policy environment that could unlock untapped potential and reduce import dependency for India's gold sector.

forces.title: Very low domestic gold production hinders self-sufficiency
forces.description: India's domestic gold production (IN020401) was only 1 tonne in CY23, representing a mere 0.02% of the world's total output. This extremely low production capacity, despite high domestic consumption, is a significant headwind for the gold mining sector, leading to heavy import reliance and missed opportunities for value creation within the country, exacerbating the supply-demand gap.

forces.title: PLI schemes and SEZs to boost domestic gold production
forces.description: Government initiatives, including establishing gold manufacturing hubs in Special Economic Zones and implementing Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes for gold ore concentrates, are designed to enhance domestic production. These policies provide significant tailwinds for the gold mining and processing sector (IN020401), aiming to lessen import reliance and achieve self-reliance under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative through targeted incentives and infrastructure development.

forces.title: Reduced customs duty on gold ore supports domestic processing
forces.description: The government's decision in July 2024 to sharply cut customs duty on gold ore from 14.35% to 5.35% is a significant tailwind for India's gold processing industry (IN020401). This move aims to curb smuggling and boost the organized market, lowering raw material costs for domestic refiners and making local gold processing more competitive and attractive for investment and output expansion.

forces.title: High import taxes and foreign equipment dependence increasing project costs
forces.description: The Indian gold mining and processing sector (IN020401) faces a significant headwind from high import taxes on equipment and a dependence on foreign machinery. These factors substantially increase project expenses and operational costs for domestic players, hindering investment and making local production less competitive compared to international benchmarks, thereby slowing sector growth and profitability.

viewpoints.title: Gold prices enter durable high-price regime driven by structural demand
viewpoints.description: Global gold prices are in a sustained high-price period, supported by structural demand shifts, continued central bank accumulation, and ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, rather than speculative flows. This creates a stable and potentially profitable environment for gold mining and refining operations, as their primary output fetches higher market prices, enhancing revenue and investment attractiveness.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

viewpoints.title: Lab-grown diamonds (LGDs) pose long-term challenges for natural diamond industry
viewpoints.description: The growing acceptance and market share of Lab-Grown Diamonds (LGDs) are reshaping consumer preferences and moderating demand for natural diamonds. This structural shift creates significant long-term challenges for the natural diamond industry, including mining (IN020404), as LGDs offer a more affordable and ethically appealing alternative, leading to downward pressure on prices and demand for rough natural diamonds.

viewpoints.title: India's gold industry faces significant supply-demand gap, relies heavily on imports
viewpoints.description: India's gold industry is characterized by a substantial supply-demand imbalance, with domestic production in CY24 meeting only 18% of total consumption. This necessitates heavy reliance on imports to fulfill internal demand, highlighting an underdeveloped domestic gold mining and processing sector (IN020401) despite India being one of the largest global gold consumers. This situation presents a structural vulnerability for the sector.

viewpoints.title: Localizing gold ore refining can yield substantial economic benefits for India
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Research emphasizes that localizing the gold ore refining industry in India, which currently relies heavily on imports (estimated at 866 tonnes in CY24), presents significant economic benefits. This strategy would lead to substantial foreign exchange savings, create numerous employment opportunities across the value chain, and boost government tax collections, fostering a self-sufficient gold processing industry (IN020401).
